description: The free, open-source part of Tactile UI: interface parts that behave like real objects. Vanilla JS and CSS, no dependencies, MIT.
readme: Tactile UI Free Interface parts that behave like the objects they are drawn from: a counter whose drums carry, a compass that settles on its bearing, a light on a pull cord. Plain JavaScript modules and CSS, no framework, no build step, no dependencies. This repo is the free, open-source part of Tactile UI: 6 pieces under the MIT licence, to use, change and ship anywhere. Piece Kind What it is Compass Object A liquid-damped compass. Live Odometer Object A mechanical drum counter. Live Pull-cord Bulb Object A pendant lamp that is a switch. Live Engraved Client Plates Block “Used in production by…”, as metal name plates. Live FAQ Index Block An FAQ as a card-index drawer. Live Machined Footer Block A footer made as the bottom panel of a device. Live Install Each piece is a folder you can copy as it is. Or add one with shadcn: npx shadcn add https://tactileui.dev/r/compass.json The registry of the free pieces is https://tactileui.dev/r/free/registry.json. The Odometer is also on npm: npm install tactile-odometer Every piece works by keyboard and touch, respects reduced motion, and stops drawing when nothing moves. The whole library What's here is a sample. Tactile UI has 23 objects, 45 blocks, 102 kit parts and 15 templates in the same language, in every finish, with React, Vue and Svelte wrappers and a custom element for each. More are free with an account; the Founder Pass opens all of it, and what comes next. Browse everything What's free and what's paid Docs Licence MIT, see LICENSE. The fonts in a piece's folder are under the SIL Open Font Licence, beside them. Everything else in Tactile UI is under the Tactile UI licence.
